To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel method for learning a forest of decision trees using a fully-corrective, regularized, greedy search.
(1) We propose a new algorithm for learning a decision forest using a fully-corrective greedy search with a novel forest structure and regularization.
(1) Regularized greedy forest (RGF), a new decision forest algorithm for learning nonlinear functions, outperforms gradient boosting on several benchmark datasets, and is competitive on others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning nonlinear functions using regularized greedy forest.

the following questions: How can we learn a decision forest that is as accurate as a single decision tree, but with many trees? What is the best way to learn a decision forest? What is the right loss function for learning decision forests?
the following questions: (1) What is the optimal forest structure for learning a set of nonlinear decision rules? (2) What is the best way to search over the space of forests?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is superior to the traditional boosting algorithms for many datasets and loss functions.
our method outperforms gradient boosting on most datasets, and vice versa on the remaining datasets.
our method is a good choice for regression and classification problems, when the data are not very high-dimensional and the number of classes is not very large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general framework for learning decision forests, and that the framework has produced better results than gradient boosting on some datasets.
our algorithm can be viewed as a regularized variant of Friedman's gradient boosting algorithm.
we are the first to show that greedy search for forests can be made to be fully-corrective and regularized, which leads to better performance in practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and efficient algorithm can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on several benchmark datasets.
it is possible to learn a nonlinear decision forest using regularized greedy search.
regularized greedy search is a general framework that can be applied to learn forests of general loss functions, and it can be used to design new tree learners.
